done_when: When a cold read or review loop stops, forge read, forge close, forge land and forge next print a ready-to-ask question that names the item in plain words and what it delivers, lists each open blocking note or finding as one plain sentence saying what goes wrong for whom, and says what accept, narrow and split would each concretely do for this item, and the guide tells the coordinator to ask exactly that

findings.body: Raise: Not done. With the default `stop_default = "narrow"`, a review-loop stop in `forge land` never prints its ready-to-ask question. Land catches the question-bearing refusal at `src/forge/land.py:55–60`; `_wait_for_choice` catches it again at lines 125–131 and prints only a generic waiting message. This new print at line 85 covers a separate three-fix-round stop. The named close test sets `stop_default = "off"`, so it passes without exercising the default path.
findings.title: Not done: forge land omits the question during a review hold with the default setting

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `plain()` retains up to two sentences from a finding body and appends both to its title, so one blocker can occupy multiple sentences instead of the required one plain sentence saying what goes wrong for whom. The named read and close tests explicitly expect two-sentence blocker lines, so they pass while this Done-when detail remains unmet.
findings.title: Not done: blocking notes and findings are not each one sentence

stop.reason: Owner rule for Harm 1-2: both findings are fixed in commit 715dee9; close re-reviews the current head

why: When a cold read or review loop stops, the owner is asked to accept, narrow or split with no context; with many items in parallel they can't tell what the item is or what was flagged
